description:
**Blocked by d06.6 (Screen root + UI.Slots registry exists),
d06.13 (dialog overlay machinery), d06.14 (selector overlay
machinery). Read deck §12 "Extension points: replacing
components" before starting.**

Follow-on to the VDom epic. Once the slot registry exists,
expose the upstream pi-mono extension surface to octo_pi
extension authors.

**Read first (upstream pi-mono — these are reference
implementations):**
- `tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts`
  — the `ExtensionUI` interface (~lines 160-205). Defines:
  `setHeader`, `setFooter`, `setWidget`, `setStatus`, `setTitle`,
  `custom`, `pasteToEditor`, `setEditorText`, `getEditorText`,
  `registerMessageRenderer`. Read the doc comments — they
  capture the contract precisely.
- `tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts`
  — line 242 `registerMessageRenderer` implementation.
- `tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts`
  — lines 1920-1925: `setExtensionFooter` /
  `setExtensionHeader` callees that the API messages are routed
  to.
- `tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/`:
  * `custom-header.ts` — replaces logo with a pi mascot.
  * `custom-footer.ts` — token/cost/branch readout.
  * `message-renderer.ts` — custom message-type rendering.
  * `widget-placement.ts` — positioned widgets.
  * `doom-overlay/` — focus-grabbing overlay.
  * `working-indicator.ts` — `setStatus` example.
- The post-d06.6 octo_pi side: `OctoPi.TUI.UI.Slots` (slot
  registry), `Components.Screen` (the root that resolves slots).

**Read also (octo_pi extension foundation):**
- `apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/` — find the existing
  Extension API module (likely `Coder.Extensions.API` or similar).
  This new module sits alongside it.

**New module:**
`apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/extensions/ui.ex`

**Public API (each function casts a message into Interactive,
which folds it into UI.State):**

  ```elixir
  @spec set_header(api :: t, mod :: module() | nil) :: :ok
  def set_header(api, mod) do
    cast(api, {:slot_override, :header, mod})
  end

  @spec set_footer(api :: t, mod :: module() | nil) :: :ok
  def set_footer(api, mod), do: cast(api, {:slot_override, :footer, mod})

  @spec set_widget(api :: t, key :: atom(), mod :: module() | nil, opts :: keyword()) :: :ok
  def set_widget(api, key, mod, opts \\ [])

  @spec register_message_renderer(api :: t, type :: String.t(), mod :: module()) :: :ok
  def register_message_renderer(api, type, mod)

  @spec set_status(api :: t, text :: String.t() | nil) :: :ok
  def set_status(api, text)

  @spec set_title(api :: t, title :: String.t()) :: :ok
  def set_title(api, title)

  @spec custom(api :: t, factory :: (map() -> module()), opts :: keyword()) :: {:ok, term()}
  def custom(api, factory, opts \\ [])
    # Focus-grabbing overlay: pushes a vhole onto the overlay slot;
    # blocks until the component calls `done(result)`. Returns the
    # result. Overlay vs non-capturing controlled by opts[:capture].
  ```

**Reconciler-side support (lands here, not in d06.2):**
- `UI.Slots.override(state, slot_id, mod_or_nil) :: state` —
  updates `state.ui.slot_overrides`, invalidates the affected
  slot id.
- `UI.MessageRenderers.register(state, type, mod) :: state`
  — extends the message-renderer registry consulted by
  `Components.Transcript` for unknown content types.
- `UI.Overlay.push(state, factory, opts) :: state` —
  pushes a focus-capturing overlay; pops on `done/1`.

**Custom message renderer dispatch:**
`Components.Transcript` already routes built-in entry types to
built-in components. Extend it: for entry types not in the
built-in map, look up the renderer registry; render the result
inside the standard transcript-entry frame (gutter + spacing).
Unmatched types fall back to a "Unrecognized message type"
diagnostic VFlow.

**Acceptance:**
- An extension can replace the header at runtime; tmux smoke:
  load the equivalent of `custom-header.ts` (port it as an
  example under `apps/octo_pi_coder/examples/extensions/` or
  `apps/octo_pi_coder/test/fixtures/`); the swap completes
  with no flicker and the original returns when the override
  is set to `nil`.
- A custom message-type renderer survives a full TUI lifecycle:
  registered → message of that type sent → rendered with the
  custom renderer → unregistered → next message of that type
  falls back to the diagnostic.
- `Coder.Extensions.UI.custom/3` shows an overlay that captures
  keys until `done/1` is called; non-capturing variant
  (`opts[:capture] = false`) leaves base focus alone.
- Test parity: port the upstream tests
  `tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/test/compaction-extensions.test.ts`,
  `extensions-input-event.test.ts`, and `overlay-options.test.ts`
  for the equivalent UI override paths. Per the
  `feedback_ape_tests` memory: when porting a TS test, scan
  the upstream test file end-to-end and recreate every assertion
  in Elixir, don't just port the implementation.
- `mix test` green; tmux smoke with at least one of: a custom
  header, a custom footer, a custom message renderer, a custom
  overlay.

**Out of scope:** The loader/discovery side of extensions
(`Coder.Extensions.Loader`) — that lives elsewhere. This ticket
is strictly about the UI plumbing exposed to already-loaded
extensions. The `custom-provider-*`, `dynamic-tools.ts`,
`event-bus.ts`, `permission-gate.ts`, etc. extension hooks under
`tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/` are
NOT the concern of this ticket — only the UI-facing ones listed
under "Read first" above.
title: Coder.Extensions.UI: wire slot registry + message renderer registry to the extension API
